title: Presence in prayer
hookLine: a heart that knows what it says

cards: A cloak with markings woven into it. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ prays in it, and during the prayer his eye catches the markings.

Afterward, a report in Sahih al-Bukhari says, he hands it back: take this to Abu Jahm, and bring me his plain one instead, because this distracted me in my prayer. A garment, given away for being too interesting.
It's a small story, and it fits anyone who has finished a prayer, or a song, or a sentence, and not heard a word of it.

teach.b: Khushu' is presence in prayer: a stillness of body and a heart that is there, humble, attending. You met it in year two; today, a closer look. First, the Qur'an puts it at the head of a list.
Surah twenty-three opens, in Pickthall's translation: "Successful indeed are the believers Who are humble in their prayers." The Arabic word behind humble shares a root with today's word.
Success begins with how a person stands in prayer. Second, the line in today's carry.
Surah four tells believers not to draw near to prayer while drunk, and Pickthall gives the reason: "till ye know that which ye utter."
The verse is about intoxication, but some readers hear in its last words what prayer is for: knowing what you're saying while you say it. Third, why the words matter.
A hadith in Sahih Muslim, in which the Prophet relates God's words, says the prayer is divided between God and the one praying, and each line of al-Fatiha gets an answer.

The person says, in Pickthall's words, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds," and God says: My servant has praised Me. "The Beneficent, the Merciful," and God says: My servant has extolled Me. Line after line.
On that hadith, al-Fatiha isn't only a recitation. It's a conversation, and one side is answering. Fourth, the cloak again.
Even the Prophet removed a distraction rather than fighting it.

teach.h: CLEAR THE ROOM, THEN BE THERE.
teach.b: So khushu' can start with the room: a plain wall, a quiet corner, the phone somewhere else.
Make it easier to be there, then be there.

how: Muslims seeking khushu' learn the meanings of what they recite, pray slowly, keep their gaze on the place of prostration, and clear distractions from the place where they pray.

o: presence in prayer: a still body and an attentive heart
reciting the Qur'an aloud in a beautiful voice
praying many extra units late into the night

games.q: you're praying in a cloak with markings, and your eye keeps catching them. what does the Prophet do in the report?
o: pray with more effort and ignore it.
give it away and ask for a plain one.
keep it: distraction is part of life.
games.why: he sent it to Abu Jahm and asked for his plain one, saying it had distracted him in his prayer (Sahih al-Bukhari).

practice: Take the first line of al-Fatiha in its meaning, praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and say it slowly inside; then leave a pause as long as the line, for the answer the hadith describes.
If you pray, you can pray one prayer today this way, even if it takes longer than usual. If you don't, sit with that first line in English and let the pause after it be real.

wordCard.voice: Khushu'. Presence in prayer: a still body, a humble heart, and knowing what you say while you say it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: humble stillness, presence of heart in prayer. the same root gives khashi'un in Qur'an 23:2.

carryVoice: Your line: know what you say. In the hadith, every line of al-Fatiha is answered. See you tomorrow.
